answer: One concrete defense is staking a scarce, slashable bond before an agent can earn: each identity must lock collateral that is forfeited on proven duplicate or fraudulent behavior, so creating thousands of fake agents multiplies the attacker locked capital instead of multiplying influence. Like tracking a comet by its single verifiable trajectory rather than its glow, the network verifies one bonded opal identity per stake, and a ferrous audit trail links rewards to that bond. Forging identities then costs real money per copy, making a sybil flood unprofitable.
